simple: This page is about changing how characters look in your game, like giving everyone a helmet, a green head, or a special outfit. You can set rules for everyone at once in Studio's Avatar Settings, or change any character with a script using a `HumanoidDescription`. The script way works on players and on NPCs. The page also explains what custom models need so layered clothing can fit them.
analogy: A `HumanoidDescription` is like a written order at a costume shop: "blue shirt, two hats, tall body". You fill in the order, then hand it to the character, and they change into it.
keyPoints: File > Avatar Settings in Studio changes clothing, body parts, animations, and more for every player character at once.
For one character or an NPC, use a `HumanoidDescription`, which lists scale, accessories, clothing, body parts, body colors, and animations.
Step 1: get a description, usually from the character with `humanoid:GetAppliedDescription()`, from an outfit ID, or from a user ID.
Step 2: change its properties, like `Torso`, `HeadColor`, or `HatAccessory`. Several accessories go in one comma-separated string.
Use `SetAccessories()` to add many accessories, including layered ones with a set order, at once.
Step 3: apply it with `humanoid:ApplyDescription()`, or spawn a player in it with `player:LoadCharacterWithHumanoidDescription()`.
To dress characters as they spawn, set `Players.CharacterAutoLoads = false` and load each character yourself.
Layered clothing on custom models needs a `WrapTarget` on the body, a `WrapLayer` on the clothing, matching cage UV maps, and a `Weld` if the model is not an R15 humanoid.

terms.HumanoidDescription: An object that describes a character's whole look: body, colors, clothes, accessories, and animations.
terms.asset ID: The number that identifies an item on Roblox, like `86500008` for a torso.
terms.comma-separated string: Several values in one piece of text split by commas, like `"2551510151,2535600138"` for two hats.
terms.scale: How big a body part is compared to normal. `1` is normal size, so `1.2` is 20% bigger.
terms.BodyTypeScale: How much the body shape leans toward a less blocky, more human-like shape. `0.1` is only a little.
terms.classic clothing: Flat images painted on the body: `Shirt`, `Pants`, and `ShirtGraphic` (a T-shirt picture).
terms.layered accessory: 3D clothing that stretches to fit over the body, like a jacket over a sweater.
terms.Order: In `SetAccessories()`, which layer goes on first. Order `1` (sweater) sits under order `2` (jacket).
terms.CharacterAutoLoads: A setting on `Players`. When `false`, Roblox does not spawn characters by itself, so your script must do it.
terms.WrapTarget: A part of a body mesh that layered clothing can wrap around.
terms.WrapLayer: A part of a clothing mesh that wraps over a `WrapTarget`.
terms.cage: An invisible simple shell around a mesh that guides how clothing stretches over it.
terms.UV map: A flat map that says which point on a 2D picture goes on which point of a 3D shape. Cages must use matching UV maps to line up.
terms.Weld: An object that locks two parts together. `Part0` and `Part1` are the two parts it joins.
terms.undefined behavior: Results nobody can promise, so things might look broken or random.

example.title: Give every player a green head when they spawn
example.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local function onCharacterAdded(character)
	local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid")

	-- Start from the look the character has right now
	local description = humanoid:GetAppliedDescription()

	-- Change only what we want
	description.HeadColor = Color3.new(0, 1, 0) -- bright green
	description.HeightScale = 1.1 -- 10% taller

	-- Put the changed look back on the character
	humanoid:ApplyDescriptionAsync(description)
end

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
	player.CharacterAdded:Connect(onCharacterAdded)
end)
explain: Each time a player's character spawns, `onCharacterAdded` runs.
`GetAppliedDescription()` copies the character's current look, so we keep their own avatar.
We change two things: head color to green and height to 1.1 times normal.
`ApplyDescriptionAsync()` puts the new look on the character. The page shows the older name `ApplyDescription()`, and the API reference says to use `ApplyDescriptionAsync()` for new work.

watchOut: Starting from `Instance.new("HumanoidDescription")` when you only want a small change. A blank description wipes the player's whole avatar. Use `GetAppliedDescription()` instead.
Changing a character's parts directly while also using `HumanoidDescription`. Mixing the two can break the look.
Setting `HatAccessory = "123"` when you meant to add a hat. That replaces all hats. Add with `.. ",123"` instead.
Expecting scale properties to work on R6 characters. They only affect R15.
